subject: POC acceptance criteria + measurement plan
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Yuan <alice.yuan@finvera.com>; Raj Patel <raj.patel@finvera.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC acceptance criteria + measurement plan

Thanks for the time today — good call. Below is a concise runbook we propose for the 4-week POC and the success criteria we’ll measure against. Please review and flag anything missing.

High-level summary
- Scope: GenAI-assisted underwriting assistant (document parsing + short-answer generation) using an open model variant (Llama-4x-8b-quant).
- Duration: 4 weeks (kickoff week + 3 weeks of evaluation).
- Environment: Redwood Dedicated dev pool in us-west (isolated instance).

Acceptance criteria (hard requirements)
1) Latency: p50 generation latency <= 120 ms; p95 <= 300 ms on the defined test traffic (see attachment).
2) Throughput: sustain at least 1,000 tokens/sec aggregate at target concurrency (10 simultaneous sessions) without QoS degradation.
3) Cost: effective cost per token (inference compute) <= $0.0025 after batching and quantization settings.
4) Quality: automated eval on the shared test set: exact-match / pass-rate >= 92% for extraction tasks; human eval mean score >= 4.0 / 5 on 150 samples for generation quality.
5) Reliability: error rate <= 0.5% (timeouts/errors) during a 24h soak run at 50% of target load.

Ownership and roles
- Finvera: provide redacted sample traffic, acceptance test set, and security contacts (SOC2/KMS requirements). Primary contact: Alice Yuan.
- Redwood: deliver POC infra, run tests, provide dashboards and scripts for reproducible measurements. Primary contacts: Marissa (deployment & monitoring), Vivek (perf tuning).

Key deliverables & timeline
- Kickoff call (30–45m): Wed Mar 4, 10:00 AM PT — setup accounts, share sensitive contacts, confirm dataset schedule.
- Data drop: Finvera to upload sample-traffic.jsonl by EOD Fri Mar 6.
- Week 1: baseline runs + tuning (quantization, batching profiles).
- Week 2: soak testing & reliability validation.
- Week 3: quality eval and human grading window.
- Final report: consolidated SLA matrix, cost breakdown, dashboards — delivered within 3 business days after week 3.

Monitoring & metrics we will provide
- Real-time latency percentiles (p50/p90/p95/p99) per route.
- Token throughput and tokens-per-second graphs.
- Cost breakdown by model/route and aggregation per 1k tokens.
- Error logs and request traces (redacted for PII).

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood-poc-runbook.pdf (PDF)], [Attachment: sample-traffic.jsonl (JSONL)]

Next steps (what I need from you)
1) Confirm kickoff time (Mar 4 at 10:00 AM PT works for you?).
2) Confirm dataset owners and expected volume (approx tokens/day).
3) Any regulatory/data-residency constraints we should be aware of.

Thanks — I’ll book the kickoff and share a calendar invite after I hear back.

—
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0198

From: Alice Yuan <alice.yuan@finvera.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@finvera.com>, Finvera Engineering Team <eng@finvera.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 16:04:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: POC acceptance criteria + measurement plan

Karthik — thanks for the thorough summary. Quick answers and a couple of constraints from our side:  

- Kickoff: Mar 4 10:00 AM PT works for our team (I’ll confirm calendar invites).
- Data residency: all sample data must remain in the us-west environment and not be replicated outside our VPC. We will redact PII but may need assistance with tokenization edge cases — will flag examples.
- Procurement: procurement is targeting a PO by end of March, so timeline is tight; we need the POC to demonstrate clear cost forecasts.

On acceptance criteria: the latency/throughput targets look reasonable. A couple of changes we’d like to request:  
1) Please also include a per-request token cap and how batching will affect tail latency — we expect some user-facing requests to be short (<50 tokens) and some to be long (~800 tokens).
2) For quality, add a secondary metric: hallucination rate measured on 200 targeted cases (acceptable threshold <= 3%).

I’ve looped Raj and the Eng team — Raj will coordinate procurement milestones. We’ll upload the first data sample (redacted) by Mar 6 EOD as discussed.

On SOC2/kms: please send SOC2 report and basic KMS integration notes ahead of the kickoff.

Thanks,
Alice
Sr. Product Manager, Finvera
alice.yuan@finvera.com

Thanks — looping in implementation details from Redwood CS/Platform perspective so there’s no ambiguity on what we’ll deliver and when.

Implementation plan (concise)
- Environment: we'll provision a dedicated dev pool in us-west with isolated networking. Access will be via SSO invite + short-lived API keys scoped to the POC.
- Test harness: we will run the sample-traffic.jsonl you provide through a reproducible runner. We’ll include a config file that defines concurrency profile (10 concurrent sessions), per-request token caps, and a blended distribution to reflect short and long requests.
- Batching & quantization: Vivek will run an initial sweep of batching window sizes (8ms, 20ms, 50ms) and two quantization profiles; we’ll provide the tradeoff matrix (latency vs cost) in the week 1 report.
- Monitoring & dashboards: out-of-the-box dashboards will include p50/p95 latency per route, live tokens/sec, error rates, and cost per 1k tokens. We’ll give you read-only access to the dashboard.
- Evaluation artifacts: sla-acceptance-matrix.xlsx with pass/fail per metric; evaluation scripts for automated reruns; a human-eval template for graders.

Owner contacts
- Marissa Cole (CS lead) — marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com — deployment and runbook owner
- Vivek Kulkarni (Performance) — vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com — perf tuning and quantization lead

Security notes
- SOC2 report and KMS integration summary will be attached to the kickoff calendar invite. We will not request any raw PII. If we need plaintext examples to reproduce tokenization issues we will provide controlled redaction guidance.

I’ll prep the initial runbook and share the onboarding steps immediately after the kickoff.

—
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
